independent_solution.calculation_or_logic:
Let the initial momentum of the light pulse be $p$ in the positive direction. The initial momentum of the stationary object is 0.

Case 1: Perfect Absorption
Initial total momentum = $p + 0 = p$.
After absorption, the light pulse has 0 momentum. The object gains momentum $p_\text{abs}$.
By conservation of momentum: $p = 0 + p_\text{abs} \implies p_\text{abs} = p$.

Case 2: Perfect Reflection
Initial total momentum = $p + 0 = p$.
After reflection, the light pulse travels in the opposite direction, so its momentum is $-p$. The object gains momentum $p_\text{refl}$.
By conservation of momentum: $p = -p + p_\text{refl} \implies p_\text{refl} = p - (-p) = 2p$.

Ratio: $p_\text{refl} / p_\text{abs} = (2p) / p = 2$.

notes: The question correctly applies the principle of conservation of momentum to a light-matter interaction.
The distinction between absorption (momentum change $p$) and reflection (momentum change $2p$) is fundamental and correctly tested.
The provided formula for photon momentum ($p=E/c$) ensures the question is self-contained and does not require prior advanced knowledge.
